key_insight: PI-GINOT learns geometry-conditioned finite-strain hyperelastic responses directly from point-cloud descriptions, enabling data-free prediction across parametric DogBone shapes.
engineering_relevance: It can reduce the need for repeated finite-element simulations in virtual testing, design optimization, and uncertainty studies when specimen geometry changes.
method: Encodes each DogBone boundary point cloud into geometry features.
Uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacement at arbitrary query points while enforcing boundary conditions exactly.

Computes stresses via automatic differentiation with a compressible Neo-Hookean plane-stress model and trains with physics constraints (equilibrium, traction-free/symmetry, stability, internal-force consistency).
evidence_signal: On eight unseen geometries, the method reports 2.1%–7.1% displacement error, 0.9%–13.3% peak von Mises stress error, and section-force error below 10.3%, with Abaqus used only for post-training validation.
watch_item: Local stress components are less accurate near the gauge-to-fillet transition, especially for narrow specimens with steep stress gradients.
paper_title: PI-GINOT: Data-free geometry-informed neural operator learning for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens
